conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. A likely revenue beat against one analyst's $7.25M bar (Q3 beat the same bar by 14%) is offset by three things: this is the first fiscal-year-end call under a new CEO, the DataSeeds pivot is funded by insiders and the buyback has been suspended, and a 10-Q shows subscription billings falling (-4.4%) while recognised subscription revenue rose 32%. So p_up is 50 and abs_move is 14% on the name's own median reaction, with no usable option chain. The finding sum (0.0) and the scaled number (0) agree.
bar: Q4 FY26 (May-Jul 2026) consensus revenue $7.25M, EPS $0.04, from one analyst (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSEAMERICAN/ZDGE/earnings/). There is no company guide. The Seeking Alpha FY26 consensus from March 2026 ($29.77M revenue, https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ZDGE/earnings/estimates) is stale and implies a lower Q4. The bar does not have two agreeing sources, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 37,971 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (66,926 at 09-15), about 0.3% of the ~13M pre-placement shares, days to cover about 1.0 (https://equibles.com/stocks/zdge/shortinterest). The short is not crowded and there is no squeeze mechanism. The option chain is unusable: ATM spread is 133% of mid, there is no 25-delta skew, and the put/call OI ratio of 2.21 rests on only 170 contracts, so it carries no directional statement. Tape: 20-day run-up -12.3% and 5-day -2.9%. Spot $2.71 is 8-9% below the $2.93/$2.98 price insiders paid in the September private placement. The buyback was suspended on 2026-08-31, so the company is no longer a bid.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 revenue should land around $7.6-8.0M against the single-analyst bar of $7.25M (+5-10%). The base is Q4 FY25 revenue of $7.5M (ad $5.2M, subscription $1.4M). Subscription revenue has grown 31-32% a year, recognised from a deferred-revenue balance of $6.2M (+26%). Marketplace ad revenue is flat on higher prices per impression. Against that, Emojipedia ad revenue fell 53%. The same analyst's Q3 bar was $7.0M and the print was $7.99M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-06-11): a 14% revenue beat against the same $7.0M bar bought +25.7% close to close, then gave almost all of it back the next session (4.16 to 3.25, per the Yahoo daily bars). Q4 FY25 (2025-10-28): flat revenue with restructuring fell -24.3%. Q2 FY26: revenue +18% with an Emojipedia impairment fell -14.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The only bar is one analyst who undershot Q3 by $1M. If the market expected a beat, the stock would not have drifted 12% in 20 days to below the insiders' September purchase price on light volume (10-60k shares a day).
findings.independence: Q4 FY25 comparison base and line split: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1667313/000121390025102776/ea026271401ex99-1_zedge.htm. Ad-pricing proxy from Alphabet's Q2 2026 10-Q (AdMob revenue up, Network cost per impression +13%): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000071/goog-20260630.htm. That is a proxy, not a company number. The MarketBeat bar is the same single source as the bar field.

findings.finding: This is the first fiscal-year-end call under new CEO Morris Berger (from 2026-10-01). He is on $450k salary plus options on 3% of shares, and the strategy has moved to building DataSeeds.AI into a core business: talent, technology, datasets and selective acquisitions, funded by the $7.675M insider placement, with the buyback suspended. The company guided to 'improved profitability and FCF' for FY26 a year ago. Any FY27 framing is now likely to be an investment year with higher opex, which works against the ~20% FCF-yield valuation case. The size of the spend has not been disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last fiscal-year-end print with forward framing (Q4 FY25, 2025-10-28) fell -24.3%. The Aug 31 pivot announcement itself traded +5.9% (2.87 to 3.04 on 949k shares) and then drifted back below $2.90.
findings.why_not_priced: The pivot is public, but there is no opex or headcount number for it anywhere: the October investor deck gives 'no specific revenue or profit targets'. If the market had priced a heavy investment year, the stock would be trading near cash rather than at a ~$15.7M EV on $3.1M TTM FCF.
findings.independence: The October 2026 investor deck (8-K 7.01) lists use of funds and the buyback suspension: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1667313/000121390026111195/ea030927101ex99-1.htm. The CEO employment terms are in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1667313/000121390026108282/ea0308225-8k_zedge.htm. All of this is company documents and no outside source. Financing check: the money is insider cash (no fees, no debt, warrants at 110%) for a business with corroborated demand (a six-figure evals contract, the Bria engagement, repeat customers), so the financing itself is not a negative. The negative sits only on the opex path, which is inference.

findings.finding: The Q3 FY26 10-Q shows subscription billings down 4.4% to $1,757K while recognised subscription revenue rose 31.9% to $1,678K. Developed-market MAU fell 17.3% to 4.3M, and those are the higher-priced subscribers. The 30%+ subscription revenue growth the release headlines is coming off deferred lifetime-subscription revenue while new billings shrink, so the growth line should decelerate. The FY 10-K and call will expose that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction is attributable to billings. MAU declines have run at -11% for several quarters (Q4 FY25 -11.1%, Q3 FY26 -11.3%) through both +25.7% and -24.3% reactions, so the market has not reliably punished MAU.
findings.why_not_priced: The billings figure is only in the 10-Q MD&A. The press release and the October investor deck headline subscription revenue +32% and active subscriptions +41%. If billings were priced, previews and the deck would not lead with the revenue growth rate.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the 5-year intangible/goodwill finding. The deferred revenue figure ($6.2M, +26%) in the Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001667313/000121390026067834/ea029448101ex99-1.htm) points the other way for near-term recognised revenue. That is why this is sized small and partly offsets F1 rather than contradicting it: F1 is Q4 revenue, F3 is the growth trajectory beyond it.

findings.finding: Insiders put $7.675M into Class B stock at $2.93-2.98 (closed 2026-09-25). Howard Jonas's Chartwell alone put in $6.5M, unborrowed, taking him to 15.6%. The stock is now $2.71, with pro-forma cash of $27.4M (~$1.75/share on ~15.7M shares) and no debt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None for this line. The placement close (2026-09-25 to 09-30) coincided with a drift from 3.09 to 2.88.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced: the stock is below the insider price on thin volume. What remains is that a cash floor near $1.75 limits the downside of a bad print more than a 14% median reaction implies, and on a thin day that could temper a negative reaction.
findings.independence: 8-K/A placement close: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1667313/000121390026104861/ea0306984-8ka1_zedge.htm. This is the same placement document set as F2's funding, but it bears on a different line (valuation floor versus opex path).

findings.finding: The fiscal-year-end impairment test is the risk window. Remaining goodwill is $2.14M and net intangibles $1.07M at 2026-04-30. GuruShots monthly active payers fell 37.7% and Emojipedia revenue fell 53% after a $3.7M impairment in Q2. Any Q4 non-cash charge is capped at about $3M, roughly 7% of market cap, below operating income, with no path to the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FY26 print that carried the $3.7M Emojipedia impairment fell -14.5%, together with an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: No one has quantified whether a year-end test triggers. If the market expected a charge, a GAAP-loss headline would not surprise. It is small in dollars either way.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as F3, so the two share a document but sit on different lines. No outside source.

findings.finding: DataSeeds signed its first six-figure model-evaluation contract (reported 2026-09-01) and completed its first commercial evals engagement for Bria.AI (press release 2026-10-19). Neither has a revenue figure. The new CEO's first call will likely use these as pipeline evidence, and they mostly fall into Q1 FY27 revenue rather than Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 FY26 print that announced DataSeeds' first six-figure order rose +25.7%. The Bria release on 2026-10-19 moved the stock 2.78 to 2.79, which is nothing.
findings.why_not_priced: Both items are public, and the 10-19 release drew no reaction. What is unpriced is any contract value or backlog figure the call might put on them, and management has repeatedly said it cannot project DataSeeds revenue.
findings.independence: The Bria engagement release: https://www.valuethemarkets.com/news/press-releases/zedges-dataseedsai-and-bria-complete-first-ai-model-evalua. It is a company-sourced press release distributed by a third party.

outside_window.finding: The placement warrants (2.35M shares at $3.22/$3.28) become exercisable only after stockholder approval and March 2027. They add dilution and an overhang above the current price, but nothing exercisable inside the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: A current Q4 consensus from a second source: Benzinga and GuruFocus returned 403, Seeking Alpha's FY consensus is dated March 2026
Q3 FY26 call transcript commentary on May-July trading: allmind.ai summary only, with no Q4 numbers given by management
News explaining the 2026-10-13/14 drop from 2.93 to 2.74: none in EDGAR or the wires (worth 0 per the lessons)
App-store rank or review trend for Zedge Ringtones/GuruShots: not searched to completion; no dated source found

rejected_candidates.candidate: Alphabet Q2 2026 10-Q: AdMob revenue up, Network cost per impression +13%, read as support for Zedge ad pricing in May-July
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into F1 (revenue beat) as a supporting proxy, so the ad-pricing fact is not counted twice.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Quarterly dividend of $0.02 continues (~3% yield), as stated in the August press release and the October deck
rejected_candidates.detail: Already folded into F2/F4 context. Continuation was stated on 2026-08-31, so declaring it with results adds nothing new.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Jonathan Reich's new President/COO agreement ($390k salary, 100k RSUs/DSUs)
rejected_candidates.detail: Part of the same leadership transition as F2. Its cost effect is immaterial and is included in the opex-path finding.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with because the chain is unusable. The -12.3% 20-day drift below the insider purchase price is consistent with a market already discounting an investment year (F2) and does not pre-price the likely revenue beat (F1), so the findings offset rather than lean.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question) and lesson 5 (inference is smaller): F2 cut from -1.5 to -1.0. The placement funds a business with corroborated demand, and the negative rests only on an undisclosed opex path, which is inference.
Lesson 5 (positioning and unexplained drawdowns in a microcap are worth about 0): F4, the stock below the insider price, cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 6 (single-source bar caps every finding): F1 was already capped at +1.5 in the draft, so it is left standing; the cap is stated in the bar field.

Lessons 1 and 8 left the scaled number alone. Abs_move stays at the name's own 14% median and p_up stays at 50, because the reaction history (+25.7% and then a full fade on a beat, -24.3% on a flat year-end) gives no reliable reaction function for the revenue line.
